title: Battle of Blood River
summary: On 16 December 1838 about 470 Voortrekkers under Andries Pretorius, formed up in a wagon laager on the Ncome River, defeated a Zulu army sent by King Dingane. SAHO gives 10,000–20,000 Zulu attackers and EBSCO about 10,000; both report about 3,000 Zulu dead and no Voortrekkers killed or almost none. The victory became central to Afrikaner national memory.

uncertainty.note: SAHO and EBSCO both give 16 December 1838.

as_recorded.value: On 16 December 1838 the Battle of Blood River took place near the Ncome River in KwaZulu Natal.
a significant battle that took place on December 16, 1838

where.modern_name: Ncome River, Nquthu / Dundee area, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa (proxy pin: Ncome Monument and Museum Complex, mapped in OpenStreetMap beside the river)
where.historical_name: Banks of the Ncome River, then Zulu kingdom under Dingane, border with Voortrekker settlement

importance.justification: EBSCO calls it a pivotal moment in Afrikaner national identity and the Great Trek narrative; it weakened the Zulu Kingdom.

audience_note: Describes a battle with about 3,000 reported dead on one side.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap Nominatim: Ncome Monument and Museum Complex (way 1530761771; -28.1057910, 30.5458490)
sources.author: OpenStreetMap contributors

reviewer_note: Casualties are quoted per source: SAHO "more than 3000 Zulu casualties", 3 Voortrekkers wounded, none killed; EBSCO "about 3,000 Zulus killed", "less than a handful of wounded". Zulu strength differs: SAHO 10 000-20 000, EBSCO 10,000. Pin is a proxy (the Ncome museum complex beside the river), not the laager site; no source I opened gives the laager coordinates.
